findings.title: New downsize overload silently shadows the 4-argument downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height)
findings.body: `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` (line 149) redefines the `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` method declared at line 145; in Ruby the later definition wins, so the 4-argument form is unreachable. Any caller passing explicit dimensions (e.g. `OptimizedImage.downsize(src, dst, 1024, 768)`) is now dispatched to the new method with `dimensions = 1024` and `opts = 768`; `optimize` then evaluates `opts[:allow_animation]` and raises `NoMethodError: undefined method '[]' for 768:Integer` instead of producing a `1024x768` instruction. Even when no exception is raised, `dimensions` is a bare Integer, yielding a broken `-resize` argument. Callers elsewhere in the codebase or scripts that use the width/height form will break silently. Remove the four-argument overload or give the string-dimensions entry point a distinct name.

findings.title: Downsizing an animated GIF keeps only the first frame when allow_animated_thumbnails is off
findings.body: The controller's new resize path calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(..., allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails)`. When that setting is false (the default), `optimize` selects `downsize_instructions`, whose command contains `#{from}[0]`, i.e. only the first frame of a multi-frame GIF. Because the downsized temp file replaces the upload, an animated GIF larger than `max_image_size_kb` is permanently stored as a static single-frame image, silently destroying the user's animation. The animated instruction set is only used when the setting is explicitly enabled. Animated uploads should either always go through the animated/`gifsicle` path or be exempted from automatic downsizing.

findings.title: Downsize loop with at most five 80% steps cannot bring files more than ~3x the limit under the limit
findings.body: Repeatedly applying `-resize 80%` five times yields only 0.8^5 ≈ 0.33 of the original, so a file more than roughly 3x `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` is still oversized after the loop and `Upload.create_for` then rejects it. The advertised feature (accept large images by shrinking them) therefore still fails for genuinely large uploads, e.g. a 10MB image on a 1MB limit. Each pass is also a separate lossy re-encode (no `-quality` specified), so intermediate steps degrade the image more than necessary. The required scale factor should be computed from `tempfile.size / limit` (or the loop should recompute a percentage from the current size) rather than using fixed 80% steps.

findings.title: Resize loop runs ImageMagick on SVG uploads, which convert cannot faithfully handle
findings.body: The guard only checks `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)`, and that helper's image list includes SVG, so an SVG larger than `max_image_size_kb` is fed to `OptimizedImage.downsize` → `convert`. `OptimizedImage.create_for` deliberately special-cases `.svg` (it copies the file instead of calling `resize`), showing that `convert` is not suitable for vector files. The result is either a rewritten/rasterized file different from what the user uploaded (data loss) or a failed `convert`; in the failure case the loop still spawns five pointless `convert` processes per upload before giving up. Exclude SVG (and any format that cannot round-trip through `convert`) from the resize loop.

findings.title: Client upload limit hard-coded to 10MB, ignoring max_image_size_kb/max_attachment_size_kb site settings
findings.body: `validateUploadedFile` previously derived the limit from `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`; it now always uses `10 * 1024` KB for both images and attachments. Attachments are not auto-downsized on the server, so sites configured with a smaller `max_attachment_size_kb` will now accept up to 10MB in the browser and only fail later with a less clear server error (or the setting is effectively bypassed). The same applies to images where an admin deliberately configured a limit below 10MB. In addition, the 413 handler at line 246 now reports `max_size_kb: 10MB` regardless of the web server's real limit, so the error message can be wrong. The limit should stay driven by the site settings (or a dedicated setting for the resize threshold).

findings.title: No tests for the new automatic downsizing behavior or the OptimizedImage API refactor
findings.body: The PR adds a multi-iteration in-place resize loop in `UploadsController#create_upload` and changes the public signatures of `OptimizedImage.resize/downsize/optimize`, but no specs were added or updated. Tests covering (a) an oversized image that must be shrunk, (b) a file that remains oversized after five attempts, (c) an animated GIF and an SVG upload, and (d) a call to `downsize` with explicit width/height would have caught the shadowed-method bug and the first-frame truncation. Please add model/controller specs for these paths.
